# Oliver Newth (n3wth.com) — Full Context for LLMs

> This file provides comprehensive context about Oliver Newth and n3wth.com for language models. For a shorter summary, see llms.txt.

## About Oliver Newth

Oliver Newth is an AI Product Lead at Google (2025 to present), developing AI platforms that integrate DeepMind models into production software.

### Contact
- Email: hey@n3wth.com
- Location: San Francisco, CA

### Professional Background
- **Google** (2025 to present): AI Product Lead. Product development for AI platforms that integrate DeepMind models into production software.
- **Covariant** (2022 – 24): Staff Product Manager. Product work on computer vision for warehouse robotics.
- **Meta** (2017 – 22): Product Manager. Ran video calling across Instagram and Portal; before that, core growth and integrity. Meta Build Social Value Award, 2020.
- **Microsoft** (2014 – 17): Product Manager, Azure. Product on Azure Cognitive Services; the job was getting enterprises to trust AI enough to adopt it.

### Education
- MEng in High Performance Structures, Massachusetts Institute of Technology (Kennedy Scholar)
- Civil Engineering, First Class, University of Warwick

### Expertise
- AI Product Strategy
- GenAI Platforms
- Autonomous Coding Agents
- Trust & Safety Systems
- Robotics and Automation

## Site Structure

### Main Pages

#### Home (https://n3wth.com/)
Who Oliver is — AI at Google, art in the desert. A 3D night field scene built by an agent team.

#### Work (https://n3wth.com/work/)
Independent AI projects and product roles at Google, Covariant, Meta, and Microsoft.

#### After Dark / Art (https://n3wth.com/art/)
Large-scale light installations for Burning Man and San Francisco memorials:
- **THEM** (2022): Lighting and Circle of Light ring. Black Rock City, Nevada. Design: Simón Malvaez. Fabrication: Brenden Blaine Darby. Fractured Atlas.
- **Pink Triangle** (2022): Project coordination as part of Illuminate on Patrick Carney's Pride memorial. Twin Peaks, San Francisco.
- **Circle of Light** (2021): World AIDS Day memorial for the National AIDS Memorial. AIDS Memorial Grove, San Francisco.

#### Thinking (https://n3wth.com/thinking/)
Positions on production AI and agents as an org-design problem, with interactive AI-safety trade-off walkthroughs.

##### Featured Thinking Pieces:
- **Agents are an org design problem** (/thinking/agents-org-design): A standing team of coding agents, each with a named desk and a real schedule. One boundary has never moved, no matter how good the model got.
- **Trust is a runtime property** (/thinking/trust-production): A policy that says harmful content never surfaces without review is enforced by a latency number, not by the document that states it.
- **AI should be present, not summoned** (/thinking/ambient-ai): The chat box makes you stop and decide what to ask. An ambient layer reads the room instead.
- **What "autonomous" actually means in production** (/thinking/autonomous-agents): Click through what an agent can take back and what it can't.
- **Why every AI-generated UI looks the same** (/thinking/ai-design-slop): Purple-to-blue gradient cards, a centered icon grid, low-contrast dark mode.
- **What the night field broke** (/thinking/night-field): The homepage's 3D scene built by an agent team — everything that went black, spun around the wrong point, or skated across the ground before it worked.
- **Compound engineering, applied to a personal site** (/thinking/compound-engineering): Five real pull requests from this site's git history showing what compounding actually looks like.
- **Tell it as a place** (/thinking/field-guide): A field guide to a site that tells your story instead of listing it.
- **A standing team with named desks** (/thinking/agent-desks): A desk on an org chart isn't real until it has a trigger, a boundary, and a timestamp.
- **How this backlog got built** (/thinking/this-page): Twenty Thinking pieces, built by parallel agents in isolated worktrees.
- **The machine that runs my todo list while I sleep** (/thinking/gtd-mini): A headless Mac Mini, a cron job every fifteen minutes, and a timeline of what it actually did.
- **Live artifacts are three different architectures** (/thinking/live-artifacts): A sandboxed page with a versioned link, a full dev environment in a browser tab, and real production component code.
- **A knowledge base becomes a graph once something else can query it** (/thinking/personal-knowledge-graph): PARA and Zettelkasten pushed back on hierarchy for a human reader. The graph shape only starts to matter once an agent can traverse it.
- **Automation is arbitration plumbing** (/thinking/home-automation): A sensor reports, a hub decides, an actuator acts.
- **The toll booth is memory, not math** (/thinking/llm-inference): Prefill runs once, in parallel. Every token after that is its own round trip to memory.
- **TypeScript at the edge** (/thinking/edge-typescript): Cloudflare Workers run TypeScript inside V8 isolates instead of VMs or containers.
- **A computed verdict can still be wrong** (/thinking/hop-flights): hop.flights' whole pitch is a verdict that's computed, not guessed.
- **Kroots: mapping a graph nobody else could see** (/thinking/kroots-map): A one-person kids'-media venture with no team still needed an org chart.
- **The toll-free verification maze** (/thinking/twilio-compliance): Twilio rejected the same toll-free application twice, for two different fields.
- **Working notes: 2026** (/thinking/2026-goals): Four generic goal categories, one review cadence each.
- **The PDF gotcha that cost an afternoon** (/thinking/pdf-charspace): A hairline rule in a table looked wrong by 10 to 25 points.

## Live Products

Products designed by Oliver, kept shipping by an autonomous agent team:

### hop.flights (https://hop.flights/)
Points-vs-cash flight optimizer — finds the cheapest way to fly, miles or money.
- Tech: Next.js, AI SDK, Duffel

### r3 (https://r3.n3wth.com/)
Memory for AI apps using vector search and knowledge graphs.
- Tech: TypeScript, Redis, Vector Embeddings, MCP
- GitHub: https://github.com/n3wth/r3

### kit (https://kit.n3wth.com/)
49 components with AI context packs. Ships your design system straight to your editor and coding agents.
- Tech: React, Tailwind v4, Radix, shadcn
- GitHub: https://github.com/n3wth/kit

### skills (https://skills.n3wth.com/)
A registry of markdown skills for coding agents. Install with one command, run locally, work offline.
- Tech: Next.js, React, Supabase
- GitHub: https://github.com/n3wth/skills

### garden (https://garden.n3wth.com/)
A digital garden of interconnected working notes. Notes carry growth stages (seedling, budding, evergreen) and are gathered into groves.
- Tech: Next.js, Astryx, Wikilinks
- Has its own llms.txt

## Technical Stack (n3wth.com)

- **Framework**: React 19 + TypeScript + Vite 7
- **Styling**: Tailwind CSS v4
- **Animation**: GSAP 3 (ScrollTrigger, SplitText)
- **UI Library**: @n3wth/ui (shared component library)
- **Fonts**: Satoshi (display), Geist Sans (body), Geist Mono (code)
- **Analytics**: PostHog (deferred load)
- **Deploy**: Vercel

## Agent Team

Oliver builds and operates independent projects with coding agents. These projects are separate from his work at Google.
